decision_time: reassessment checkpoint — after current result/state/treatment updates
purpose: Minimum safe level of care at the current reassessment checkpoint.
design_notes: Agent 4 does not re-diagnose sepsis, repeat workup decisions, or re-decide initial treatment.
Disposition terminals are exactly discharge, observation, ward, ICU.
cannot_determine is not a disposition; it is represented as status=abstain with disposition=null.
SSC 2026 has no ED disposition scope for Agent 4. Reasons must be grounded in current checkpoint/upstream fields, not fabricated guideline citations.
D1 Tier A ICU hard safety triggers are deterministic and cannot be overridden by the model.
Tier B ICU candidate criteria are pending clinical sign-off and inactive as hard gates by default.
Supplemental oxygen alone, chronic pre-encounter tracheostomy, sep3, SOFA >= 2, high NEWS, and derived sep3_shock are not independent deterministic ICU triggers.
insufficient_evidence is routed only through Yana's V4 insufficiency logic; there is no generic insufficient_evidence -> observation fallback.
Any valid carried insufficient-evidence state prevents final discharge through the uncertainty ceiling.
JSON graph controls ordinary D2/D3/D4 transitions. Deterministic code intentionally controls D0 data validation, D1 ICU hard safety gate, V4 insufficiency routing, and the uncertainty ceiling.
D4 answer=yes requires a non-null, non-empty escalation_trigger; this dependency is explicit in the node prompt and remains validator-enforced.
In current v0.2 routing, valid insufficiency usually terminates immediately as observation or abstain; the uncertainty ceiling is retained as a secondary/future-proof safeguard.

icu_hard_triggers.description: Vasopressor already in use: setting in {ed, pre_arrival} and observed start_time <= checkpoint cutoff.
Invasive ventilation during the current encounter with starttime <= checkpoint cutoff.
Non-invasive ventilation or HFNC during the current encounter with starttime <= checkpoint cutoff.

icu_candidate_triggers_tier_b.description: 30 mL/kg initial resuscitation completed and post-resuscitation vital_map_min < 65.
Lactate value >= 4 mmol/L with sample time after initial resuscitation.

icu_gate_governance.source: Yana agent4_disposition_graph v0.3-draft; semantically ported into RADAR vNext

D1.title: ICU hard safety gate
D1.question: Does the patient meet any hard ICU safety trigger by the current checkpoint cutoff?

D2.title: Continued inpatient-level need
D2.question: Does the patient still require hospital-level treatment or monitoring that cannot be safely provided through observation or discharge?

D3.title: Observation-specific need
D3.question: Is there a genuine short-term, resolvable uncertainty or monitoring need that prevents discharge but does not require ward or ICU care?

D4.title: Discharge safety
D4.question: Is discharge currently safe based on the available checkpoint and upstream information?
D4.transition_note: A no answer at D4 means discharge is not supported after the graph has already rejected ward and observation pathways. It does not authorize a free-form fallback disposition; the system abstains unless a prior node has established a non-discharge terminal.
